subject: Singapore
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Singapore Airlines Flights 23 and 24. The route is drawn on the great circle between the two cities; the flown paths are described, not drawn.

claims.text: Singapore Airlines Flights 23 and 24 are the longest regularly scheduled non-stop flights in the world, between Singapore Changi Airport and New York–JFK.
The route has a great circle distance of 15,349 kilometres.
SQ24 to New York is typically flown a ground distance of around 17,250 km over the Pacific Ocean where jet stream winds can assist.
SQ23 back to Singapore sometimes opts, instead of the westward polar route, to fly eastward across the Atlantic Ocean when favourable jet stream winds assist.
The flights are scheduled to take over 19 hours and 18 hours respectively.
